messages:
lee: FYI I'm seeing a throughput regression on A100 rigs for long sequences (>>1024). Autotuner keeps picking a tile=128 / smem=48k kernel and perf tanks with lots of stalls. nvprof shows register spills + low active warps.

sana: Can you paste the autotune pick log and a tiny repro harness? Also: is KV-cache involved or is this the cold path?

lee: Repro: 8xA100, batch=1, seq=1536, model=redwood-v1-ish, kv-cache=enabled (prefix hit ~70%). Autotune excerpt below: 
```
[autotune] candidates: ker_tile64_sm96_reg40, ker_tile128_sm48_reg48, ker_tile192_sm32_reg56
[pick] selected: ker_tile128_sm48_reg48 score=0.71 est_latency=42ms
[profile] observed p50=78ms p95=153ms reg_spill_pages=3 l2_bw=62GB/s
```

matt: I grabbed HW counters during the slow run: 
```
SM_active_warps_avg=10.7 / 32 theoretical
registers_per_thread=48 -> spill to local mem (~12 pages)
local_mem_bw=200GB/s
smem_util=55% (configured 48k)
```
Seems the chosen kernel has higher regs/thread and the autotune model underestimates the spill penalty at this seq len. Occupancy is way down.

ashley: Two quick ideas: (1) Add a spill-penalty term to the autotuner cost model that grows with registers_per_thread and seq_len (spill_bytes * mem_latency_coefficient). (2) Ensure the candidate set always includes an occupancy-friendly kernel (e.g., tile64 with lower regs/unroll) as a fallback for long sequences and KV-heavy workloads. We already have warp-specialized fast paths for <512; mirror that idea for >1024 but inverted.

lee: I forced ker_tile64_sm96_reg40 locally via env override and throughput improved ~1.9x at seq=1536. Latency variance increased a bit but p95 dropped from 153ms to ~95ms. Command I used: 
```
export RUNTIME_KERNELS_ALLOW='["ker_tile64_sm96_reg40"]' && ./runtime_harness --model redwood-v1-ish --seq 1536
```

runtime-bot: autotune-job queued for model redwood-v1-ish seq=1536 on 8xA100, will run exhaustive candidate profiling and update policy if persistent.

sana: Next steps: (A) add spill penalty to cost function, tune coefficient on perf microbenchmarks; (B) add explicit occupancy-favoring candidate to default pool for seq>1024; (C) run a KV-cache sweep to see interaction with prefix hit rates (70% might hide cold-path costs). I'll spin up a small experiment matrix.

matt: I'll add a perf counter hook to the autotuner so picks that cause local_mem_bw > threshold are penalized. Also we should record reg_spill_pages in the telemetry event for later analysis.

ashley: If we add the fallback kernel, consider a gradual rollout (canary 5% traffic) and add an eval that runs synthetic KV traces to ensure quality and jitter bounds.

lee: Sounds good. Saving logs to s3://redwood-perf/1716427890/ and attaching repro to the autotune ticket. Thanks all.
